answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: to harbor real standing, an agent must stake tokens and earn endorsements over time, while a fresh identity starts with nothing. Attackers can wander in with a thousand sock puppets, but each puppet pays the same bond and waits out the same aging period, so cost scales linearly with fake identities. A nebula of cheap clones collapses because no clone inherits the history that makes trust valuable.
